F: Primary study synthesis. Findings and recommendations retain draft status.

1.6.intro: Unit training connects prior learning to performance in a particular operational setting. Its output depends on training opportunities, instructors, assessment and progression—not just the number of trainees entering.
1.6.heading: Where the bottleneck can arise
items: Operational staffing pressure can reduce the staff available to instruct.
Limited instructor availability can constrain training throughput.
Slower qualification delays the replenishment of the operational workforce.
1.6.limit: This feedback chain is an Atlas synthesis of mechanisms discussed in the study, not a separately quantified feedback model.
1.6.source: F: sections 2.3 and 4.3, Annex F. I: chapter 2.

2.6.intro: Workforce supply evolves through inflows, outflows and training lead times. More training intake today is not the same as more qualified operational staff today.
2.6.heading: Read the supply chain
items: Training intake, duration and success determine the timing and scale of new qualification.
Retirements and other attrition reduce the available workforce.
Transfers change local supply; they need not increase total European supply.
2.6.limit: Transfers are shown here as a boundary consideration, not asserted to be an explicit variable in the final report model.
2.6.source: F: section 2.2 and Annex E. I: chapter 4 (earlier model version).

3.4.intro: A response to constrained unit-training output can combine instructor resources, training design and the scheduling of training opportunities.
3.4.heading: An intervention portfolio to examine
items: Dedicated instructor functions or instructor and assessor pools.
Competency-based progression and suitable preparation before operational training.
Monitoring completion, duration and operational staffing effects together.
3.4.limit: This is an illustrative combination, not a package with a demonstrated combined effect. The study’s “Best Practice” label is not by itself proof of effectiveness.
3.4.source: F: sections 4.2–4.4 and Annexes G–K. Portfolio grouping: Atlas proposal.

4.6.intro: The workshop proposes three domains to distinguish what might transfer between settings and what may need further training and assessment.
4.6.heading: Three domains, integrated performance
items: Core ATCO competence — common foundations of controller work.
Technical-system competence — competence with the relevant system and human–machine interface.
Operational-environment competence — competence for the relevant traffic, procedures and operating conditions.
4.6.limit: The domains form a conceptual model, not an additive equation. Recognition still requires evidence of integrated performance under defined conditions.
4.6.source: W: slides 5–16. C: CBL one pager.

4.8.intro: Training and assessment establish evidence of competence. Formal recognition asks what that evidence authorises, in which conditions, and with what boundaries.
4.8.heading: Keep the concepts distinct
items: Proposed competency-based licensing concerns the basis for formal recognition.
System-based licensing and non-geographic validation are related options requiring their own definitions.
Cross-border service provision is an operational arrangement, not a synonym for a licensing model.
4.8.limit: These are proposals for exploration. Regulatory records require verification against the instruments before publication.
4.8.source: W: slides 5–16. C: CBL one pager. F: sections 4.3.3–4.3.4.

refContent: Canonical definitions
Workforce gap: demand minus supply, within the model’s stated scope and units.
Training intake, recruitment applications and successful selection are separate quantities.
Headcount, FTE, operational hours and utilisation require explicit definitions before comparison.
Definition records should preserve differences in source usage.
Regulation and policy records
Instrument and provision
Jurisdiction, applicability date and version
Current requirement versus proposed change
Detailed regulatory records have not been verified for this preview.
Actors and responsibilities
ANSPs: workforce planning, training resources and operational deployment.
Training providers: learning programmes and training capacity.
Authorities: relevant approval and oversight responsibilities.
European and national actors: coordination and enabling frameworks.
Illustrative actor mapping; responsibilities must be linked to the relevant measure and instrument.
Source records
A source document and a finding extracted from it are separate records.
Case study records
Operational setting and reported problem
Practice introduced and implementation conditions
Reported outcomes, evidence quality and transferability limits
Case narratives remain to be populated from the supplied reports.
Initiatives
FINEST: locate within future operating concepts; preserve source-dated status.
EXODUS: the supplied intermediate report leaves substantive coverage for later completion.
Initiative existence is not evidence of a demonstrated workforce effect.
Technology records
Function and task affected
Human responsibility and degraded-mode behaviour
Training implications and source-reported maturity
Technology descriptions should connect to tasks before drawing conclusions about competence or staffing.
Model and data records
Final draft: supply–demand projection to 2036.
Intermediate report: earlier outlook to 2040.
Keep coverage, granularity, units, assumptions and version alongside every result.
Do not combine the two model versions into one continuous forecast.

steps.label: Pipeline
steps.q: Why might more intake fail to produce more qualified ATCOs?
steps.body: Unit training needs instructor time, assessment and suitable operational opportunities. These resources can constrain throughput.

steps.label: Shortage
steps.q: How does this affect the supply outlook?
steps.body: Intake enters a training process with duration and success assumptions. Constrained progression can delay workforce replenishment.

steps.label: Solutions
steps.body: Examine instructor capacity, training preparation and scheduling together. Increasing intake alone may leave the constraint in place.

steps.label: Future ATCO
steps.q: What changes when training or recognition is redesigned?
steps.body: Identify which competence can transfer and which system or operating-environment differences still need training and assessment.
